atomic.title: Structure of the Atom and Radioactivity

questions.text: The word 'atom' is derived from the Greek word 'Atomos,' which means:
questions.explain: Atomos in Greek means something that cannot be divided.

questions.text: The subatomic particle with a negative charge is the:
questions.explain: Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus.

questions.text: The mass of an atom is primarily concentrated in the:
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons, which carry almost all the mass, are located in the nucleus.

questions.text: Who discovered the nucleus through the Gold Foil experiment?
questions.explain: Rutherford's gold foil experiment led to the discovery of the dense central nucleus.

questions.text: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the 'L' shell is:
questions.explain: Using the 2n² formula, for L-shell (n=2), max electrons = 2(2)² = 8.

questions.text: Neutrons were discovered by:
questions.explain: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.text: The atomic number (Z) represents the number of:
questions.explain: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.

questions.text: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of:
questions.explain: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to neutrons.

questions.text: Natural radioactivity was discovered by:
questions.explain: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while working with uranium salts.

questions.text: Which of the following radiations has the highest ionizing power?
questions.explain: Alpha particles are relatively heavy and double-charged, giving them high ionizing power.

questions.text: The process in which a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei is called:
questions.explain: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into smaller ones with energy release.

questions.text: The isotope used for the treatment of cancer is:
questions.explain: Cobalt-60 produces gamma rays used to treat cancer (radiotherapy).

questions.text: Carbon-14 dating is used to determine the age of:
questions.explain: Carbon-14 dating estimates the age of organic materials like fossils.

questions.text: Alpha particles are identical to the nucleus of:
questions.explain: An alpha particle consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons, same as a Helium nucleus.

questions.text: The SI unit of radioactivity is the:
questions.explain: The Becquerel (Bq) is the SI unit, named after Henri Becquerel.

questions.text: Nuclear Fusion occurs naturally in:
questions.explain: Fusion of hydrogen into helium is the primary energy source for stars.

questions.text: Which material is commonly used as a moderator in nuclear reactors?
questions.explain: Moderators slow down neutrons to sustain a chain reaction.
